description:
FILED s523 (Fable, 2026-10-20 23:0x) at s522b's MERGE-READY question.  s522b shipped, under the s522 ruling (b), a rule-12 DEATH for deleting a non-sub stash symbol; it cost 7 perl rows that passed only because the operation was a silent no-op (perl-tests/ref.t 200 `freeing freed glob in global destruction`; t/mro/basic.t 51 63 64 66 -- `delete *main::x` / `delete *Foo::ISA`; t/op/stash.t #128086 and `%A::=""` -- the announcement rows).  RULED s523 (DECIDED ## s523): the death is WITHDRAWN -- an effect-only miss ANNOUNCES and continues (the s329 boundary); perl's own pinned-glob rule makes "compiled accesses keep working" RIGHT.  THIS TASK is the real answer: the delete records the symbol as GONE in the one side table the sub-removal path already uses (s522b's `p-delete`-on-a-stash write-through + the stash memo), so `keys %Pkg::`, `exists *Pkg::x`, `scalar %Pkg::` and a SYMBOLIC lookup `` / `` / `defined &{"Pkg::x"}` answer as perl (gone; a symbolic lookup after the delete autovivifies a NEW cell distinct from the compiled one -- probe perl: `our  = 1; delete *main::x; print  // "undef"` = undef, then ` = 2; print ` = 1 -- the compiled `` is the OLD cell), while compiled `` / `` keep their cell.  `delete` RETURNS the glob (perl: the deleted typeglob value; `my  = delete *main::x; *` still reaches the old cell) -- the view's glob answer from s522b's "a non-CODE element reads as its typeglob" is the thing to return.  Shapes to probe vs perl first (10 min): the three above; `delete *Foo::ISA` then `` (compiled, keeps) vs `` (gone) vs method resolution (perl: the MRO sees the pinned array? -- PROBE: mro/basic.t 51-66 are exactly this, read them); a filehandle symbol; `local *main::x` (out of scope: the deferral); global destruction order (ref.t 200).  Layer: cl/ (`p-delete`'s stash arm + the stash view + the symbolic-lookup resolver; ONE side table, rule 11).  Acceptance: the 7 rows back to passing WITHOUT the announcement, the stash-hash-01 guard rows, not-supported.md's "Live symbol-table hashes" edited again.  Parent: #3511 / #1510 (DONE under the bounded ruling).

=== DONE (s523d, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-22, commit 7bc42e50) ===
cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `%p-stash-delete-glob`, called from p-delete's stash arm in place of s522b's announcement: the glob's package's OWN `$name` / `@name` / `%name` symbols are UNINTERNED.  CL gives perl's pinned-glob model exactly: compiled code holds the symbol objects and keeps the old cells, while every run-time lookup by NAME (the stash view's do-symbols, exists, the symbolic resolver, every `(find-symbol "@isa" pkg)` reader -> isa / method resolution) misses, and a later symbolic write interns a FRESH variable.  The symref name memo is cleared; a per-site symref cache re-checks `(symbol-package sym)` (an uninterned symbol re-resolves) -- one slot read on the cached path.  delete returns the glob.  A same-name FILEHANDLE stays (announced, effect-only); a name that is both a sub and a variable deletes only the sub (the element's value is the code ref) -- both written into not-supported.md "Live symbol-table hashes".
Probes (scratch/s523d/pr/sd.pl + sd/a-f.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs tree): exists / keys / `${"main::x"}` undef then a new cell (`$x $$r ${'main::x'}` = `1 1 2`), `Blength->isa("Bladd")` 1 -> 0 after `delete $Blength::{ISA}`, mro/basic.t's three fresh_perl ISA programs, ref.t 200's program, `delete $s->{ISA}` through `\%Fake::`, deleted @a / %h -- ALL identical to perl, no stderr.  Guard Pl/t/stash-hash-01.t r9 (rewritten from the announcement assertion to perl's answer) + r10 (inverse: base fails both).  Acceptance rows (ref.t 200, mro/basic.t 51/63/64/66, op/stash.t 2): the sweep + the companion one-file runs, see s523d STOP.md.
